readout_other: Dynamic numeric rating scale for knee pain; Brief Pain Inventory; WOMAC; light-touch sensation; quadriceps strength (Oxford scale)
direction_notes: Mean dynamic NRS fell in all groups including sham; the 225 W/cm2 group reported larger reductions than the 150 W/cm2 group, but the authors state no conclusions can be drawn with n=7.
safety_notes: No device-related cutaneous irritation, systemic side effects or other adverse events; sensation and quadriceps strength were not decreased.

exposures.label: Single 15 s sonication of the infrapatellar branch of the saphenous nerve at 150 or 225 W/cm2

target.label: infrapatellar branch of the saphenous nerve

device.model: Resonance (driven by a signal generator and power amplifier, Model H-107, Sonic Concepts)

timing.protocol_description: Participants received one 15 s focused ultrasound (or sham) treatment after which the transducer was removed; intensity was scaled for overlying fat and muscle attenuation. Cohorts were 0 (sham), 150 or 225 W/cm2 spatial-peak temporal-average, randomised 1:2:2.

source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Participants underwent focused ultrasound (or sham) treatment for 15 seconds (pulse duration) with a peak acoustic pressure of 2.2 MPa, after which the transducer was removed.
source_quotes.n_subjects: Due to the limited sample size ${ \bf { \dot { n } } } = 7$ with 5 receiving active treatment), no conclusions may be drawn regarding effectiveness or safety; but this firstin-humans use of low-intensity focused ultrasound to treat pain does suggest that continuing study is warranted.
source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.pressure: Participants underwent focused ultrasound (or sham) treatment for 15 seconds (pulse duration) with a peak acoustic pressure of 2.2 MPa, after which the transducer was removed.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: Participants underwent focused ultrasound (or sham) treatment for 15 seconds (pulse duration) with a peak acoustic pressure of 2.2 MPa, after which the transducer was removed.
source_quotes.exposures[0].in_situ.ispta_w_cm2: It remains unknown if the doses used in the current study (150 and 225 $\mathrm { W } / { \mathrm { c m } } ^ { 2 }$ for 15 seconds) were adequate and/or optimal.

flags.reason: The paper calls the 15 s a 'pulse duration'; recorded as sonication duration, pulse duration left not_reported.
Spatial-peak temporal-average intensity given as 150 and 225 W/cm2 (18 W, 27 W); the text says it was scaled for attenuation but does not say whether it applies in water or at the nerve.
The device is Pegasus Resonance; the Sonic Concepts H-107 is named in the sentence as the driver but the transducer maker is not stated explicitly.
No frequency is stated in the text.
Sham is 0 W/cm2 treatment; how it was produced is not described.
